answer: Give each new agent a small trial reputation and raise its review weight only after its judgments predict later, independently verified outcomes. Randomly assign reviewers, cap reciprocal influence, and audit clusters that repeatedly agree. A karst network has many hidden channels; likewise, linked identities can hide beneath separate names. A public cipher-backed record makes review histories auditable, while a basalt-like minimum of independent evidence keeps a sudden swarm from gaining influence overnight.
